result:
All 59 tests pass and `defects4j compile` succeeds.

Created `gson/src/test/java/com/google/gson/stream/JsonWriterAgentTest.java` (package `com.google.gson.stream`, JUnit 3 style via `junit.framework.TestCase`, matching `JsonReaderTest`'s conventions). It covers:

- Constructor null-check, default/getter/setter state (`isLenient`, `isHtmlSafe`, `getSerializeNulls`)
- Happy-path arrays/objects, nesting, method chaining, deep nesting (stack growth past initial capacity of 32)
- All `value(...)` overloads (String, boolean, Boolean, double, long, Number), `nullValue()`, `jsonValue()`, including null-argument behavior
- `setSerializeNulls(false)` semantics (omits null object members, still emits null array elements)
- String escaping (control chars, quotes, backslash) and HTML-safe escaping
- Indentation (`setIndent`) and reverting to compact output
- Lenient vs. strict mode: multiple top-level values, non-finite doubles/Numbers
- Error cases: dangling name after `name()`, name outside object (deferred check surfaces on next value write), nesting mismatches on `endArray`/`endObject`, incomplete-document `close()`, closed-writer state (`flush`, `beginArray`, `name`)

Two initial assumptions were wrong and caught by the verification run: `name()` doesn't validate context until the next value is written (deferred), and strict mode only rejects the *second* top-level scalar value, not the first — both tests were corrected to match actual runtime behavior.
